 :: JUDGMENT:

: 
The petition is filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.8,50,000/ for the grievous injuries sustained by her, in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case of the Petitioner is as follows:
That on 2772020 at about 10.30 a.m. when the petitioner was riding moped bearing reg.No.KA04JW8362 slowly, carefully and cautiously by following traffic rules on left side of the road on Mathikere main road, Mathikere bus stop, Bangalore city, Bangalore, at that time, driver of the auto bearing reg.no.KA02AB0477 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's moped, as a result of which petitioner sustained fracture of lateral condyle of left tibia, abrasion over the right anterior aspect of the leg and other injuries all over the body.

That immediately petitioner was shifted to Sumathi hospital, Bangalore wherein she took first aid treatment, thereafter she was shifted to V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala wherein she was admitted as inpatient for 25 days and surgery was done and incurred Rs.1,50,000/ towards medicine, treatment, conveyance,
attendant charges etc.,
Due to accidental injuries petitioner is suffering from permanent disability.
That prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as tailor and earning Rs.25,000/p.m. and due to accidental injuries she lost her income.

Hence petitioner prays to award compensation of Rs.8,50,000/
from the respondents.

3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1RC owner of the auto remained exparte and respondent No.2 insurer of the offending vehicle has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.

4. Respondent No.2 in written statement stated that this respondent has issued a liability only policy for commercial vehicle policy bearing No.OG2017011831 00004263 In favour of first respondent in respect of autorickshaw bearing No.KA02AB477 and it is valid from 15102019 to 14102020 and their liability, if any is strictly in terms and conditions, exceptions, limits and endorsement of the policy and subject to compliance of 64VB of insurance Act and law governing thereto.
That the first respondent had violated the mandatory provisions i.e., Section 134(c) and section 158(6) of MV Act 1989.

That the owner/insured and jurisdictional police ought to have intimated about the alleged accident to the insurer of the motor vehicle which involved in the Rekha N vs Murugesh on 7 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133837927/
2 accident as required under the aforesaid provisions.
That they have failed to comply with the section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
That after lapse of one day, the petitioner has filed a false case against insured vehicle to cause wrongful loss to this respondent.
That it is clear breach of terms and conditions of policy and also violation of section 149(2) of MV Act 1988.
That accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding the motor cycle by the petitioner herself who did not have DL and not wearing the safety helmet.

Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
5.

On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
:: ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, on 2772020 at about 10.30 a.m. while petitioner was rider in moped bearing No.KA04JW8362, when she reached HMT main road, Mattikere bus stop, Bengaluru city, at that time, a driver of the auto bearing reg.No.KA02AB0477 driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's moped, as a result of which petitioner sustained grievous injury, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whetherpetitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,
from which respondent ?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the above said issues, Petitioner has been examined as PW1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 documents.
One Dr.Manjunath Biradar got examined as PW2 and got marked ExP21 to 24.

One Dr.Nagaraj B.N. got examined as PW3 and got marked Ex P25 and 26.
8.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the Petitioner and respondent No.2.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 REASONS  Issue No.1:
10.

In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner herself entered into the witness box and filed her affidavit in lieu of examinationinchief and got examined as P.W.1 and got marked ExP1 to 19.

PW1 reiterates the averments and the allegations made in the claim petition and Rekha N vs Murugesh on 7 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133837927/
3 deposed that, the accident has occurred solely due to the negligent driving of the auto bearing reg.No.KA02AB0477.
11.
The main defence of the respondent No.2 is that he denied entire case of petitioner and specifically contended that there is a delay of one day in lodging complaint, the petitioner has not having DL.
That first respondent had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective DL to drive the same as on the date of accident.
That first respondent allowed to ply his vehicle on the road without possessing valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident.
12. In order to prove the case of petitioner, the petitioner placed reliance on police records and medical records.
On perusal of the same, this complaint lodged by petitioner on 2872020 and case registered against offending auto driver bearing No.KA02AB0477 u/s 279, 337 of IPC, 134 B r/w 187 MV Act.

The informant stated in complaint/FIS that on 2772020 at about 10.30 a.m.,
when she was going on her scooter bearing KA04JW8362, BEL circle to HMT main road, at Mattikere bus stop driver of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA02AB0477 came with high speed and negligent manner and dashed against her, as a result of which she fell down and sustained injuries to her left leg and scooter also damaged, thereafter public were shifted her from the said auto to Sumathi hospital wherein xray was done and informed doctor was not available, then for better treatment, she was admitted as inpatient at V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala.
Therefore petitioner lodged complaint on 2872020.
Accordingly the SHO of Yashwanthpur traffic police recorded FIR and proceed to conduct investigation.

The investigation officer proceeded to spot and conduct spot panchanama and filed charge sheet against driver of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA 02AB 0477 for the offence punishable u/s 337, 338 of IPC Section 134(B) r/w section 187 IMV Act.
13.

On perusal of police records and medical records, it discloses that petitioner had sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA02AB 0477 and took treatment at Sumathi hospital, Bangalore and VP Magnus hospital, Nelamangala wherein found that petitioner had sustained fracture of lateral condyle of left tibia, abrasion over the right anterior aspect of the leg and other injuries to all over the body.

14. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 15. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of evidence of PW1 coupled with contents of documents and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved this issue by producing proper documents.
Accordingly, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2: Loss of future earnings due to permanent disability :
The petitioner states that in the said accident, she sustained fracture lateral condyle of left tibia, partial thickness tear ACL with Rekha N vs Murugesh on 7 April, 2022

4 avulsion fracture tibial intercondylor eminence, comminuted mildly displaced fracture tibia and fibula, avulsion injury patellar tendon and other injuries to all over the body and shifted to Sumathi hospital Bangalore wherein she took first aid treatment and thereafter was shifted to Magnus hospital, Nelamangala wherein admitted as inpatient for 10 Days and surgery was done and discharged with an advice of the doctor, petitioner has taken followup treatment at same hospital and other hospital.
That the petitioner also taken physiotherapy for 8 months.
The petitioner has produced ExP12MRI scan report, exP13 discharge summary, ExP14la report, ExP15x rays(3), Ex P17CT scan film(4).
The petitioner has examined Dr.Manjuanth Biradar working at V.P.Magnus hospital has produced ExP21authorisation letter, ExP22police intimation, Ex P23MLC extract and ExP24case sheet.
Further petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N.Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS who has stated that petitioner had sustained left tibial condyle fracture.

That as per discharge summary, petitioner was treated at V.P.Magnus hospital with open reduction and internal fixation with plate and screws and later discharged, she was on regular followup in the same hospital and petitioner now complains of unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg, unable to pedal the tailoring machine and carry her profession as tailor.
That on examination petitioner has healed surgical scar over the left proximal leg, restricted left knee movements.
That recent x ray of the left leg shows untied fracture of the tibial condyle with implant in situ.
That petitioner had physical disability of left lower limb at 38% and for the wholebody at 13%.
That he produced ExP25clinical report and ExP26xray.
PW3 in his cross examination has stated that he is not a treated doctor to petitioner.
That he had not seen any other medical records, old xrays photocopies.
That there is no complication in fracture site.
There is no shortening of limbs.
PW3 further admitted that range of movement of hip and ankle is normal.
He assessed physical disability, not avocational disability.
Due to this accident, petitioner sustained injury in lower limb tibia.
After conservative treatment, fractures are completely united and there is no complication.
The doctor assessed wholebody disability 13%, but on consideration of present health status of petitioner, it appears to be excessive.
Hence this tribunal did not accept entire evidence of PW3.
No there could be some extent of disability faced throughout her life.
Hence considering the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, 5% disability would be taken for calculation of disability.
That the petitioner has produced ExP13discharge summary which discloses petitioner was aged 46 years at the time of accident.
The appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 is 13.
The petitioner has stated that she was Tailor by profession and earning Rs.25,000/p.m.
But the petitioner has not produced any document to prove her avocation and income.
The petitioner herself gave statement before police officer, she herself stated in ExP1 that she was a house wife, she never stated her avocation before police officer.
Then she stated in the petition, she doing tailoring work and earning Rs.25,000/p.m.
During course of cross examination, this fact was effectively cross examined by respondent No.2, she clearly admitted she studied upto PUC, she had no document to show her avocation and income.
So in the absence of material document regarding her avocation and income, it would proper to workout notional income.
The present accident occurred in the year 2020.

As per the recent decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case between MFA 4893/2016(MV) Smt.Yashodamma Vs M.D., BMTC disposed on 1610 2020 (DB) held that in case no document produced by the petitioners to prove their avocation and income, in such a situation, court can refer or rely the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority to assess notional income of injured.

Hence, as per the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dt.13082020, the notional income of Rekha N vs Murugesh on 7 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133837927/
5 the injured is taken as Rs.14,500/.
Therefore Notional Income of Rs.14,500/ p.m.

The loss of future earnings due to permanent disability is calculated as Rs.14,500/ x 12 x 13 x 5%=
Rs.1,13,100/.
17.
Pain and sufferings :

The petitioner states that in the said accident, she sustained fracture lateral condyle of left tibia, partial thickness tear ACL with avulsion fracture tibial intercondylor eminence, comminuted mildly displaced fracture tibia and fibula, avulsion injury patellar tendon and other injuries to all over the body.
That the petitioner underwent surgery.
That the petitioner now complains of unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg, unable to pedal the tailoring machine and carry her profession as tailor.

So far as the compensation under non pecuniary damages,
considering the fact that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 5% due to the accident which cause to her immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am opinion that an amount of Rs.10,000/ would be just and fair compensation under the head of pain and sufferings.
18. Loss of Amenities of Life :

The petitioner had sustained fracture lateral condyle of left tibia,
partial thickness tear ACL with avulsion fracture tibial intercondylor eminence, comminuted mildly displaced fracture tibia and fibula, avulsion injury patellar tendon and other injuries to all over the body.
That the petitioner underwent surgery.
That the petitioner now complains of unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg, unable to pedal the tailoring machine and carry her profession as tailor.
For loss of amenities of life, undoubtedly she has to lead her life ahead and she is sure to suffer on her day today activities.
Hence petitioner is awarded Rs.10,000/ under loss of amenities of life.
19. Medical Expenses:

The petitioner has stated that she spent Rs.1,50,000/ towards medicine,
treatment.
The petitioner has produced ExP9medical bills (19) Rs.1,09,826/, ExP10advance receipts (2), ExP11medical prescriptions (3).
From the medical records produced by the petitioner, it discloses that petitioner took treatment at V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala as inpatient from 2772020 to 3072020 and underwent surgery.
On perusal of ExP9, it indicates that the petitioner paid Rs.82,600/.
The hospital authorities gave discount of Rs.350/.
But petitioner claimed Rs.82,950/.
ExP9, Sl.No. 2 to 3 and 7 to 13, 16 have not contained relevant prescriptions.
The petitioner has produced invoice No.23246 dt.2872020 for amount of Rs.263=38, four common invoices produced.
On perusal of ExP24case record indicates doctor prescribed some medicines on 287 2020.
The above bills covered in ExP9 in the head of OT consumables,implant charges on 3072020 a sum of Rs.9,450/.
This amount comes in Rs.82,600/.
Therefore the said amount trying to claim again by the petitioner.
Therefore this tribunal did not grant discount amount of Rs.350/ and Rs.9,000/.
On perusal of ExP9, it indicates that in final bill, Rs.9,000/ charged for OT consumables.
Though petitioner produced some medical bills and claimed again OT consumables.
This amount was double calculated by petitioner.
Hence deduct the double calculated amount of rs.9,000/ and discount amount of Rs.350/.
ExP10 was advance bill, it was also covered in final bill i.e., on in ExP9.

Hence petitioner entitle only Rs.82,600/ +10,500+1306+224+250+300+200 grand total Rs.95,380/.
Hence

by considering the nature of injury sustained the petitioner, considering the medical bills,
awarding of Rs.95,380/ towards medical expenses would be justified.

6 20.
Food and nourishment, Conveyance and Attendant charges:

The petitioner has stated that during her hospitalization, she looked after by an attendant and incurred Rs.350/per day towards food expenses etc, she incurred Rs.350/ per day and spent Rs.35,000/ towards attendant and special dieting.
That the petitioner was shifted from Bangalore to Nelamangala and to her native place by private car for which she spent Rs.10,000/ for rent of the said car.
That she visited the hospital once in a week and spent Rs.2,800/ per trip and Rs.25,000/ for car fare.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove her above said statement nor examined the person who attended her during the course of treatment.

However in the absence of material documents, by considering the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of Rs.12,000/ under the head of Food and nourishment, Conveyance and Attendant charges.
21. Loss of income during the period of treatment:
The petitioner has stated that she was working as Tailor and earning Rs.25,000/p.m.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove her avocation and income.

The petitioner has produced ExP13 discharge summary which discloses that she took treatment as inpatient for 4 days and undergone surgery in V.P.Magnus hospital,
Nelamangala.

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment, considering 4 days admitted in the hospital as inpatient and around 60 days for rest is considered and loss of earning during treatment calculated for 60 days, notional monthly income of the petitioner is already considered as Rs.14,500/p.m. and hence loss of earning during treatment would be Rs.29,000/ under the head Loss of income during the period of treatment.
22. Future medical expenses:

It is the case of the petitioner that due to this accident, she sustained injuries as per wound certificate and she underwent surgery with open reduction and internal fixation with plate and screws and later discharged.
She examined PW3 he deposed before this tribunal that he examined petitioner clinically, radiologically recently, it appears from the xray report implants in the body of the petitioner.
PW3 deposed that she needs another surgery for removal of the implants, the estimation of this surgery around Rs.60,000/.
The counsel for respondent No.2 cross examined PW3 on this fact during course cross examination, PW3 admitted that he has not given any estimation for removal of implants.

PW3 not a treated doctor,
though treated doctor available in the hospital, petitioner failed to examine treated doctor before this tribunal.
So as per Ex P25, ExP26, implants still in the body of petitioner, so it needs to remove after sometime.
Hence considering the present status of petitioner's health condition, it is just and proper to grant Rs.15,000/ future medical expense for removal of implants and it cannot carry any interest.

23. In view of the above reasoning, petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following Heads:
SL.NO. HEAD COMPENSATION  AWARDED

1 Loss of future earnings due Rs. 1,13,100/
 to permanent disability 2. Pain and sufferings Rs. 10,000/
3. Loss of amenities of life Rs. 10,000/
4 . Medical expenses Rs. 95,380/

7

5 Food, nourishment, Rs. 12,000/
 conveyance and attender  charges 6 Loss of income during the Rs. 29,000/
 period of treatment 7
Future medical expenses Rs. 15,000/

TOTAL COMPENSATION Rs.2,84,480/
 AWARDED The said total amount of Rs.2,84,480/ is rounded off to Rs.2,84,500/.
Thus, the petitioners is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.2,84,500/ only.

24. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in a recent decision reported in 2018 ACJ 1300 between Mangla Ram V/s. Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., and others (in CA Nos.2499 of 2018 arising out of SLP(C) Nos.2814142 of 2017 decided on 06.04.2018) wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court with regard to interest at the rate of 9% p.a. on the compensation amount, in para No.28 of the judgment held that, 'The appellant would also be entitled to interest on the total amount of compensation at the rate of 9 per cent per annum on the compensation from the date of filing of the claim petition till date of realization" and also by following the principles laid down in (2018) ACJ 1020 in between ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s. Ajay Kumar Mohanty and another decided on 6.3.2018 (in CA Nos.7181 of 2015 and 1879 of 2016) at para No.1 and 12 Hon'ble Supreme Court held that: "Quantum InterestTribunal allowed interest at the rate of 7.5 per cent which was reduced by High Court to 7 per centApex Court allowed interest at 9 per cent per annum from the date of filing of claim application".

entities.text: Mangla Ram V/s. Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s. Ajay Kumar Mohanty and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above judgments with regard to the rate of interest and also it is settled principles of law that, while awarding interest on the compensation amount, the Court has to take into account the rate of interest on the Nationalized Bank and the rate of interest at the rate of 9% p.a. cannot said to be on the higher side.

Accordingly,
the Petitioner is entitled to interest at the rate of 9% p.a.
25.

Coming to the question of fixing the liability to pay the compensation to the Petitioner, it is held supra by this Tribunal that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the auto by its driver.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner, respondent No.2 is the insurer of auto are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.2 in is answered partly in the Affirmative.
26. Issue No.3 : In the result, I proceed to pass the following : : ORDER :
The claim petition filed by the petitioner u/s 166 of the MV Act is allowed in part.

The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay total compensation of Rs.2,84,500/
to the petitioner along with interest on Rs.2,69,500/ at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till deposit of entire amount tribunal.

8

After deposit of the compensation amount, the petitioner shall deposit 25% of the awarded amount as FD in any nationalised or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years and remaining 75% along with entire interest shall be disbursed to the petitioner and future medical expenses of Rs.15,000/ shall not carry any interest.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

The appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 is 13.
But the petitioner has not produced any document to prove her avocation and income.
Then she stated in the petition, she doing tailoring work and earning Rs.25,000/p.m.
During course of cross examination, this fact was effectively cross examined by respondent No.2, she clearly admitted she studied upto PUC, she had no document to show her avocation and income.
So in the absence of material document regarding her avocation and income, it would proper to workout notional income.

24. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in a recent decision reported in 2018 ACJ 1300 between Mangla Ram V/s. Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., and others (in CA Nos.2499 of 2018 arising out of SLP(C) Nos.2814142 of 2017 decided on 06.04.2018) wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court with regard to interest at the rate of 9% p.a. on the compensation amount, in para No.28 of the judgment held that, 'The appellant would also be entitled to interest on the total amount of compensation at the rate of 9 per cent per annum on the compensation from the date of filing of the claim petition till date of realization" and also by following the principles laid down in (2018) ACJ 1020 in between ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s. Ajay Kumar Mohanty and another decided on 6.3.2018 (in CA Nos.7181 of 2015 and 1879 of 2016) at para No.1 and 12 Hon'ble Supreme Court held that: "Quantum InterestTribunal allowed interest at the rate of 7.5 per cent which was reduced by High Court to 7 per centApex Court allowed interest at 9 per cent per annum from the date of filing of claim application".
In view of the above judgments with regard to the rate of interest and also it is settled principles of law that, while awarding interest on the compensation amount, the Court has to take into account the rate of interest on the Nationalized Bank and the rate of interest at the rate of 9% p.a. cannot said to be on the higher side.
